h: Moshe Speaks Through the Living Words of Torah

p: אֵלֶּה הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּיבֵּר מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹ׳ (דְּבָרִים א, א)
"These are the words that Moshe spoke," etc. (Devarim 1:1).
בְּתַנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (תַּנְחוּמָא דְּבָרִים א)
In the Tanchuma at the beginning of this parshah (Tanchuma Devarim 1):
of the King of kings of kings, etc.,
that He performed for Yisrael in the wilderness,
so will He perform for them in Tziyon.
In the wilderness it is written:
and regarding Tziyon it is written (Yeshayahu 42:16):
'I will make darkness into light before them,
and crooked places into a plain;
these are the things I have done,
and I have not forsaken them.'"
that were said about the wilderness and about Tziyon.
But the main connection to this parshah
is the pasuk "These are the words."
Now this needs to be understood:
"These are the words" of this parshah
whereas regarding Tziyon, "these are the things I have done"
so what is the resemblance of one to the other?
that "These are the words" of this parshah
One, that they are Mishneh Torah,
and it is the beginning of the Torah
which is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
"And Moshe said them on his own,"
"He explained it to them in seventy languages."
"She has hewn out her seven pillars"
"these are the seven days of Creation"
and as is written in the holy Zohar
which corresponds to Shabbos the Queen,
"She has hewn out her seven pillars"
and this book is the seventh book,
corresponding to the middah of Malchus,
that there are written in this book
the second set of the Dibros,
that there should be in them halachos," etc.,
And second, "These are the words" is expounded
as referring to words of rebuke
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסִפְרֵי, הוּבָא בְּרַשִׁ״י; סִפְרֵי דְּבָרִים א)
(as is written in the Sifrei, brought in Rashi; Sifrei Devarim 1).
in the expression "These are the words,"
in the name of the Yehudi HaKadosh, of blessed memory,
from the book of Mishneh Torah,
for he said that it served him as a sefer mussar.
Are there not many sifrei mussar?
אַךְ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הַתַּנְיָא
But it is according to what the Tanya wrote:
from the mouth of a living rebuker
is that at the time of speaking
it comes out of the heart,
and through this it enters the heart.
Now the expression "These are the words"
is like the expression "This is the word,"
except that there it is in the singular
And we said, on what they said in the Sifrei
(פָּרָשַׁת מַטּוֹת, הוּבָא בְּרַשִׁ״י; סִפְרֵי בְּמִדְבַּר קנג)
(Parshas Matos, brought in Rashi; Sifrei Bamidbar 153):
for he prophesied with 'This is the word'"
meaning that at the time when
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, said this,
from the mouth of HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
and not like the prophecy of the other prophets,
which is said in the language "So says Hashem,"
in which he relates what Hashem Yisbarach said.
"These are the words that Moshe spoke"
in the words of Mishneh Torah,
is like one who hears now from the mouth of Moshe,
through the mouth of the reader.
And the words of Moshe are
"This is the word that Hashem commanded,"
that goes forth from My mouth:
it shall not return to Me empty"

p: And this is the distinction of the words of rebuke
for it is written "These are the words":
now through the mouth of the reader.
So too regarding Tziyon it is written:
"I will make darkness into light before them,
and crooked places into a plain."
the light that was created on the first day,
which HaKadosh Baruch Hu hid away
for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh," etc.
"'He has set me in dark places' (Eichah 3:6)
this is the Talmud of Bavel";
is the aspect of the "dew of Atika,"
in that one merits to bring out
which serve to straighten the crooked heart,
as they said in the Gemara (Berachos 59a):
to straighten the crookedness of the heart,
that they should fear before Him.'"
that comes to repair the "abundance of anger";
they would have been given only
the five Chumashim of the Torah"
וְזֶהוּ אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא)
And this is "Light is sown for the tzaddik" (Tehillim 97:11)
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קסו, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
(as is written in Zohar II, end of 166b),
which is the abundance of wisdom.
(end of the first chapter of Taanis, 15a):
for to the tzaddik Hashem Yisbarach shines into him
and since he merits the light,
for he merits to straighten the heart
as it is written: "and joy for the upright of heart"
And this is also included in the pasuk
"these are the things" said regarding Tziyon,
And it says "I have done them and I have not forsaken them,"
is the words of the living God,
and likewise the words of rebuke
are "My word that goes forth from My mouth:
it shall not return to Me empty,
the crooked places become a plain.
that he speaks and it is
in the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem,"
as has been explained many times;
and he merits Torah she'b'al peh,
as is written in the holy Zohar
"and joy for the upright of heart."

paragraphs.text: Source: Koheles 3:14 — “ידעתי כי כל אשר יעשה האלהים הוא יהיה לעולם עליו אין להוסיף וממנו אין לגרע והאלהים עשה שיראו מלפניו” — “I realized, too, that whatever God has brought to pass will recur evermore: Nothing can be added to it And nothing taken from it—and God has brought to pass that mortals feel reverence.”
